articles.title: Pods as Workers, Not Agents: Rethinking the Deployment Unit for AI Agents on Kubernetes
articles.reason: This article presents a practical approach to optimizing AI agent deployment on Kubernetes, which is directly relevant for building scalable, cost-effective agentic workflows in enterprise environments.
articles.summary: The article discusses why assigning each AI agent its own Kubernetes Pod is inefficient, especially for bursty, short-lived, or hierarchical agent workloads. It introduces the kagent project and agent-substrate, which use a control plane to schedule multiple logical agents ('Actors') onto long-lived worker Pods, improving resource utilization and orchestration. This approach can inform how the consultant structures multi-agent pipelines for enterprise clients, especially when deploying on Azure Kubernetes Service.
actionable_insights: Evaluate the kagent and agent-substrate approach for current or planned multi-agent deployments on Azure Kubernetes Service.
Review existing agent orchestration patterns to identify potential resource savings by consolidating agents onto shared Pods.
Consider adapting the control plane scheduling model to improve scalability and cost efficiency in production RAG or agentic workflows.
